metaTitle: Drywall Hole Repair in Glendale, CA | $200–$365
metaDescription: Fix drywall holes in Glendale hillside homes or mid-century apartments. Flat rate $200–$365. See what causes holes and what a pro actually does.
intro: A hole in your drywall in Glendale might come from a doorknob punching through a bedroom wall or settling cracks common in the city's hillside homes. Left alone, small holes can widen or let moisture and pests into the wall cavity, especially in older mid-century apartment buildings with original plaster-and-drywall combinations.
causes: A doorknob or furniture corner impacts the wall and punches through, especially in narrow hallways typical of mid-century apartment layouts.
Hillside homes settle over time on sloped lots, which stresses drywall seams and can crack or dent the surface near corners.
Old anchors, hooks, or shelving hardware get removed and leave a hole larger than the original fastener.
Plumbing or electrical work behind the wall requires cutting an access hole that needs patching afterward.
Moisture from a slow leak softens the drywall, causing it to crumble or cave in around the damaged area.
whatProDoes: Cuts back any crumbling or water-damaged drywall to a clean, stable edge before patching.
Installs a backing piece or a self-adhesive mesh patch sized to the hole, depending on how large it is.
Applies joint compound in thin layers, letting each coat dry before sanding smooth.
Feathers the edges of the patch into the surrounding wall so the repair isn't visible once painted.
Primes the patched area and applies matching paint if requested, since Tarea pros can quote this separately.
diyOrPro: A small nail hole or dent is reasonable to patch yourself with spackle and a putty knife. Anything larger than a fist, near plumbing or electrical lines, or showing signs of water damage or mold should go to a professional, since cutting into a wall without knowing what's behind it can be risky in older Glendale buildings with outdated wiring.
priceNote: This job runs $200 to $365 in Glendale, based on an $83 per hour rate and typical jobs taking 2 to 4 hours. The time varies with hole size, how many patches are needed, and whether matching texture or paint is involved.

faqs.q: Will the patch match my wall's texture exactly?
faqs.a: A pro will try to match existing texture, but older mid-century buildings sometimes have unique plaster textures that are hard to replicate perfectly by hand.

faqs.q: Do I need to paint after the repair?
faqs.a: Yes, the patched area typically needs primer and paint to blend in, and this can be added to the job if you want the pro to handle it.

faqs.q: What if there's more damage once the wall is opened up?
faqs.a: If the pro finds water damage, mold, or wiring issues behind the drywall, they'll stop and let you know before proceeding, since that may require a different type of repair.
